chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Abu Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Sabbah al-Azraq, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:

Indeed, the most severe situation for the people on the Day of Resurrection is that the owner of the khums will stand up and say: 'O Lord, [here is] my khums, and we had purified it for our Shias so that their offspring may be pure and their children may grow.'

key_terms.لِتَطِيبَ وِلاَدَتُهُمْ: So that their offspring may be pure
key_terms.لِيَزْكُوَ أَوْلَادُهُمْ: So that their children may grow/become abundant

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of khums on the Day of Resurrection according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Imam highlights the profound eschatological significance of khums, portraying the payer as a distinguished figure on the Day of Resurrection who presents his share as a means of spiritual purification. The hadith emphasizes that khums is not merely a financial transaction but a divine mechanism to ensure the sanctity of one's lineage and the growth of offspring, reflecting the Shia view of khums as a tool for holistic spiritual and material well-being. This underscores the unique status of the Ahl al-Bayt in receiving khums to facilitate the purity of their followers' lives.
